holidays.name: No Pants Day
holidays.description: Every first Friday in May... actually, every May 1, people around the world celebrate by ditching their trousers in the name of freedom, fun, and breezy legs. Think boxers, skirts, and kilts, or just a very confident commute.
holidays.origin: The observance began in the 1990s as a lighthearted prank-turned-tradition. It grew from a small gathering of friends in the Northeast US into a global event, with the best-known ride being the No Pants Subway Ride that began in New York City in 2002.
holidays.funFact: The No Pants Subway Ride began in 2002 with just seven friends on a New York City subway train. It grew into an international event held in dozens of cities.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Parfait Day
holidays.description: A day to honor layers of glorious chocolate, cream, and crunchy bits stacked in a tall glass. Grab a long spoon and dig all the way down to the bottom.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, enjoyed by dessert lovers each May 1.
holidays.funFact: The word parfait is French for perfect, which is a fair description of a dessert that is mostly chocolate.

holidays.name: National Mother Goose Day
holidays.description: A day for nursery rhymes, storytelling, and sharing classic rhymes like Humpty Dumpty and Jack and Jill with the little ones in your life.
holidays.origin: The day was created by children's author and educator Gloria T. Delamar, who proposed it in her 1987 book about Mother Goose. It was designed to celebrate nursery rhymes and the joy of reading to children.
holidays.funFact: Mother Goose rhymes have been passed down for centuries, and many were printed in English collections well before the 1800s. Some are even thought to have roots in old folk traditions.
